source_text: Sed Paterniani iidemque Venustiani haeretici similes Manichaeis, dicunt a lumbis usque ad pedes diabolum fecisse corpus hominis, superiores vero partes Deum velut supra basem aliquam collocasse: adduntque nihil ab hominis studio requiri, quam ut anima quam in stomacho et capite habitare dicunt, munda servetur: pubem vero si omnium flagitiorum sordibus oblinatur, aiunt ad suam non pertinere curam. Ita semper ut ipsi libidini turpiter serviant, titulum ei propriae potestatis affigunt. Cuius cognatione sententiae
pass_a_gloss: But Paterniani iidemque Venustiani heretics similes Manichaeis, they-say from lumbis even-to to pedes diabolum fecisse body of-the-human, higher but partes God as-if above basem aliquam collocasse: adduntque nothing from of-the-human studio requiri, than/which so-that/as soul than/which in stomacho and capite habitare they-say, munda servetur: pubem but if of-all flagitiorum sordibus oblinatur, they-say to his-own not pertinere why. so always so-that/as themselves libidini turpiter serviant, titulum to-him propriae power affigunt. whose cognatione of-the-position.

lemmas.lexica: Blaise Manichaeus; Julian's polemic label vs natural evil
LS anima; Blaise human soul as image

pass_b_english: The Paternian heretics, also called Venustians, are like the Manichaeans. They say the devil made the human body from the loins to the feet, while God placed the upper parts upon it as though upon a base. They add that human effort requires only keeping the soul clean, which they say lives in the stomach and head. If the pubic region is smeared with the filth of every shameful act, they say this is no concern of theirs. Thus, to serve lust disgracefully themselves, they always assign it a title of independent power.

choices.why: Julian's standing charge: natural evil is Manichaean. Keep the sect-name, not 'dualists'.
Augustine's quoted claim that the unbaptized remain under the devil; keep the personal devil, not 'evil'.
rejected: under Satan (name not in the Latin here)

choices.why: Image of God in the soul; keep soul not 'mind' or 'life-force'.

anf_compare.notes: Victorian English of some of Julian survives inside NPNF Augustine (chiefly On Marriage and Concupiscence and related anti-Pelagian books). NPNF was not copied. Pass A is a literal gloss of Augustinus.it Latin of Julian's words only; Augustine's replies in the same locus are excluded. Julian is not first-English.

speaker: Julian of Eclanum (words preserved in Augustine, Contra Iulianum / Against Julian), including authorities Julian quoted; Augustine's reply at this locus is excluded.
